subject.name: Chemistry
subject.description: Cambridge International AS & A Level Chemistry. AS Level students take Papers 1 and 2 (topics 1–22); A Level students also take Paper 4 (topics 23–37). Calculations use values from the Cambridge Data Booklet. The practical papers (3 and 5) are not included. The questions are original practice questions written in the style of Cambridge papers, not reproduced past paper material.

topics.title: An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry
Chemical energetics
topics.summary: Lattice energy, Born–Haber cycles, entropy and Gibbs free energy.

topics.title: Electrochemistry
topics.summary: Electrolysis, standard electrode potentials, the Nernst equation.

topics.title: Equilibria
topics.summary: Acids and bases, pH, buffers, solubility product, partition coefficients.

topics.title: Reaction kinetics
topics.summary: Rate equations, orders, half-life, mechanisms, catalysis.

topics.title: Group 2
topics.summary: Thermal stability and solubility of Group 2 compounds.

topics.title: Chemistry of transition elements
topics.summary: Properties, complexes, colour and redox of transition elements.

topics.title: An introduction to A Level organic chemistry
topics.summary: Formulae and isomerism, including optical isomerism and arenes.

topics.title: Nitrogen compounds
topics.summary: Amines, phenylamine, azo compounds, amides, amino acids.

topics.title: Analytical techniques
topics.summary: Thin-layer and gas chromatography, carbon-13 and proton NMR.

parts.prompt: How many neutrons are in the ion ⁸¹Br⁻?
parts.examinerComment: Neutrons = nucleon number − proton number = 81 − 35. The charge does not affect the nucleus.

parts.prompt: What is the Mᵣ of hydrated copper(II) sulfate, CuSO₄•5H₂O?
What is the shape of an ammonia molecule?
parts.examinerComment: Three bonding pairs and one lone pair give a trigonal pyramidal shape with a bond angle of about 107°.

parts.prompt: Which is an assumption of the ideal gas model?

markingPoints.text: B – There are no intermolecular forces.

parts.examinerComment: Real gases deviate most at high pressure and low temperature.

parts.prompt: Which process is always exothermic?
parts.examinerComment: Energy is released when bonds form.

parts.prompt: What is the oxidation number of manganese in KMnO₄?
What is the effect of adding a catalyst to a system at equilibrium?

options.text: The position of equilibrium moves to the right.
The position of equilibrium moves to the left.
Equilibrium is reached faster but its position does not change.

markingPoints.text: C – Equilibrium is reached faster but its position does not change.

parts.examinerComment: A catalyst speeds up the forward and reverse reactions equally.

parts.prompt: How does a catalyst increase the rate of a reaction?

options.text: It increases the energy of the molecules.
It provides an alternative route with a lower activation energy.
It increases the number of collisions.

markingPoints.text: B – It provides an alternative route with a lower activation energy.

parts.prompt: How does the atomic radius change across Period 3 from sodium to chlorine?
parts.examinerComment: Nuclear charge increases while shielding stays similar, so electrons are pulled closer.

parts.prompt: How does the solubility of the Group 2 hydroxides change down the group?
parts.examinerComment: Contrast this with the sulfates, whose solubility decreases down the group.

parts.prompt: How does the volatility of the halogens change down Group 17?
parts.examinerComment: Stronger instantaneous dipole–induced dipole forces raise the boiling point.

parts.prompt: Why is nitrogen gas unreactive?

options.text: The N≡N triple bond is very strong.
It has a full outer shell.

markingPoints.text: C – The N≡N triple bond is very strong.

parts.prompt: Which functional group is present in propanone, CH₃COCH₃?

parts.examinerComment: Ethanolic NaOH favours elimination to give ethene.

parts.examinerComment: Secondary alcohols are oxidised to ketones.

parts.prompt: Which compounds give an orange precipitate with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNPH)?
parts.examinerComment: Tollens' reagent is then used to tell aldehydes from ketones.

parts.prompt: Which gas is produced when ethanoic acid reacts with sodium carbonate?

parts.prompt: What type of polymer is poly(ethene)?

options.text: steam with H₃PO₄ catalyst, then heat under reflux with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇
hydrogen with nickel, then chlorine in UV light
